react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on a primary biological signal: perturbation of Galactose Metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA (SMPDB/KEGG/WikiPathways/Reactome) ranked SMPDB:SMP00043 "Galactose Metabolism" at rank 1 (FDR = 1.65e-12, 5 of 31 pathway members hit) and KEGG:map00052 at rank 2 (same FDR, fold enrichment 1089.5). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00052 at rank 0 with p = 5.16e-08, hitting the same five compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis ranked the MUMM:galactose_metabolism module at rank 4 (p = 0.00193, overlap size 10 of 11 compounds) and MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism at rank 5 (p = 0.00294), confirming sucrose as a central input node. The five driver metabolites driving this consensus are galactitol (KEGG:C01697, the characteristic polyol of galactose dysregulation), myo-inositol (C00137, linked via galactinol synthesis), sucrose (C00089, upstream disaccharide feed), galactinol (C01235, the galactosyl donor in the Leloir pathway), and glycerol (C00116, a downstream product and hub connecting galactose catabolism to central carbon metabolism). Glycerol additionally anchors a secondary convergent theme: Glycerophospholipid metabolism, which appeared in RaMP (WP:WP2533 "Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway", FDR = 2.48e-05; REACT:R-HSA-1483206 rank 5, FDR = 1.21e-04) and Mummichog (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism rank 2, p = 0.000924), with choline (C00114) and O-phosphoethanolamine (C00346) as additional drivers. Guanabenz (C07034, an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist) did not annotate to any of the enriched pathways, consistent with its xenobiotic nature. Butanone (C02845) and 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109) contributed to minor hits in valine/leucine/isoleucine metabolism (MetaboAnalystR rank 1, p = 0.0108). The biological story is one of coordinated galactose-carbon shunting: sucrose is cleaved to hexoses that enter the Leloir pathway, whose intermediates and downstream products (galactitol, myo-inositol via galactinol, and glycerol) accumulate differentially; simultaneously, glycerol released from galactose catabolism is redirected toward glycerophospholipid and phosphatidylinositol metabolism, with choline and O-phosphoethanolamine reflecting altered membrane-lipid biosynthesis or turnover.
